title: Gene mutations; Cystic fibrosis: from gene to symptoms; Monohybrid inheritance and Punnett squares
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: GE08#t4 term and clue written for the game; GE08#t2 term and clue written for the game; GE06b#t2 term and clue written for the game; GE06b#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: GE06b#N.10, GE08#N.3, IN01#N.3, GE06b#N.14, GE08#N.12, IN01#N.8b, IN01#N.10, IN01#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Cilia
items.clue: Structures that sweep thin mucus away along a healthy airway.

items.label: Carrier
items.clue: Person with one working and one faulty allele, who has no symptoms.

items.label: Spontaneous mutation
items.clue: Permanent copying error that escaped correction, arising with no harmful agent present.

items.label: Mutagen
items.clue: Agent that raises the rate at which DNA base changes arise, without picking which gene.

questions.stem: Why is gene mutation described as the original source of all genetic variation?

options.text: Crossing over in meiosis creates new alleles, and mutation adds to the variation they produce
Most mutations are beneficial, so each one adds a useful new variant to the species
New alleles arise only by mutation; meiosis and fertilisation just recombine alleles that already exist
Organisms generate new alleles whenever their environment demands a new trait from them

questions.explanation: Every allele of every gene began as a mutation in a germ cell of some ancestor. Meiosis and fertilisation produce new combinations but cannot produce a new allele.

questions.stem: F508del removes three bases, one complete codon, from the CFTR gene. Which statement best explains why the protein fails?

options.text: Every amino acid after position 508 is changed, because the deletion shifts the reading frame.
One amino acid is missing, so the protein misfolds and is broken down.
One amino acid out of about 1480 is too small a change to matter, so the protein works normally.
A deletion stops the gene being transcribed, so no CFTR mRNA is made.

questions.explanation: Losing phenylalanine 508 changes the primary structure, so the 3D shape is wrong. Misfolded CFTR is destroyed, so few channels reach the membrane.

questions.stem: In peas the allele T for tall stems is dominant to the allele t for dwarf stems, and TT and Tt plants are equally tall. What is the reason that the heterozygote is not shorter than the homozygous dominant plant?

options.text: The T allele switches off the t allele in the heterozygote, so the plant effectively has two working T alleles
Tall plants are more common than dwarf plants, so the tall allele is the stronger one and takes over
One T allele makes enough functional protein for full stem growth, so the t allele has no observable effect
The heterozygote is in fact slightly shorter, because a single T allele makes half as much of the protein as two

questions.stem: When a new insecticide was first used on a crop, it killed nearly all individuals of a hypothetical pest insect. After several years of use, most of the pest population was resistant. Which statement best explains how resistance became common?

options.text: The insecticide caused the mutations for resistance that the insects needed to survive its use.
Insects that survived a dose built up resistance in their bodies and passed it to their offspring.
Every insect in the population gradually became more resistant until the whole population was.
Insects that already had resistance alleles from a random mutation survived and reproduced more.

questions.stem: In some people with CF, the CFTR protein reaches the cell surface membrane but its channel rarely opens. A drug that holds these channels open for longer has been developed. For a person with this type of mutation, which prediction is best supported?

options.text: The drug corrects the faulty allele, so the person's children will not inherit CF from them.
The drug will help people with two F508del alleles just as much, because they have the same disease.
Mucus becomes thicker, because more chloride in the mucus draws water out of it.
Airway mucus becomes less sticky and the sweat becomes less salty.

questions.explanation: Open channels restore Cl⁻ movement in both directions it should go: out into airway mucus, so water follows by osmosis, and back from sweat. Every downstream effect improves.

questions.stem: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele of an autosomal gene. Two parents who are both heterozygous for this gene have three children, all of whom have cystic fibrosis. Which statement correctly describes the probability that their fourth child will have cystic fibrosis?

options.text: It is 1/4, because each child's genotype is independent of the others'.
It is 1/256, because four affected children in a row would be very unlikely.
It is 1, because all three of the couple's earlier children have been affected.
It is 1/2, because the child will either have cystic fibrosis or not have it.

questions.explanation: Each child receives c from each heterozygous parent with probability 1/2, so P(cc) = 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4. The three earlier children do not change this probability.

questions.stem: To find out whether a purple-flowered pea plant is homozygous (PP) or heterozygous (Pp), a breeder crosses it with a white-flowered plant (pp). Why is a white-flowered plant used for this test cross?

options.text: Its white colour dilutes the purple, so the shade of the offspring shows the purple plant's genotype.
It passes on only p, so each offspring's colour shows the allele it received from the purple plant.
It has no allele for flower colour, so the offspring carry the purple plant's alleles alone.
It passes on both of its p alleles, so every offspring is white unless it also receives P.

questions.stem: In mice, the allele B for black fur is dominant to the allele b for brown fur. A black mouse of unknown genotype is crossed with a brown mouse. Of the 9 offspring, 5 are black and 4 are brown. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: The black mouse is BB, because a mouse that shows the dominant trait must be homozygous.
The genotype cannot be decided, because 5 : 4 is not exactly the 1 : 1 expected from a test cross.
The black mouse is Bb, because each brown offspring must have received b from it.
The black mouse is BB, and the brown offspring arose from new mutations in its gametes.
